          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
We have heard the learned counsel appearing for
the parties.

--- Page 408 ---
2
Learned counsel appearing for the petitioner
submits that the matter may be disposed of in terms
of the settlement agreement dated 22.07.2026 entered
between the parties, filed in IA No.29147/2026. He
further submits that the petitioner is having the
requisite demand draft for a sum of Rs.75 lakh. 
However, placing reliance on the order passed by
this Court it is submitted that the stamp duty on the
said agreement may be waived. The respondent is
willing to accept the aforesaid amount, provided that
either  the  petitioner  pays  the  stamp  duty  or
appropriate orders are passed by this Court for
waiving of the same.
Upon hearing the learned counsel appearing for
the parties, prima  facie, we are of the view that
Section 17(2)(vi) of the Registration Act, 1908 which
deals with the exemption from payment of stamp duty
is not applicable to a settlement agreement.
Admittedly,  we  are  dealing  with  a  case  of
compromise.
Learned counsel appearing for the petitioner
seeks further time.
List the matter next week.

--- Page 409 ---
3
In the meantime, the demand draft for the sum of
Rs.75 lakh is directed to be deposited with the
Registry of this Court.

KALPANA                                       Respondent(s)
O R D E R 
1. Leave granted.
2. This appeal is filed against the order dated
27.03.2026 passed by the High Court of Delhi in RFA
No. 287 of 2026.
3. The appellants had filed an original suit for
possession  and  permanent  injunction  against  the
respondent.  The prayer in the suit also encompassed
the claim for mesne profits.  The Trial Court, by its
judgment dated 16.11.2024, while allowing the prayer
for possession and injunction, did not grant the
relief of mesne profits.  The Review Petition filed by
the appellants has also been dismissed vide order
dated 22.08.2025.
4. Thereafter, the appellants filed a First Appeal
before the High Court, which came to be dismissed on
the ground of delay of 81 days vide impugned order
dated 27.03.2026.  The appellants sought to explain
the delay on the ground that the time was consumed in
pursuing the Review Petition before the Trial Court.

--- Page 441 ---
2
However, the endeavour to get the delay condoned was
of no avail.
5. Heard  Ms.  Deepika  Mishra,  learned  counsel
appearing for the appellants.  None appears on behalf
of the respondent despite completion of service.
6. Having considered the matter in detail, in the
facts and circumstances of the case, sufficient cause
for condonation of delay of 81 days in filing the
First Appeal is made out.
7. In view of above, the order passed by the High
Court is set aside, restoring the First Appeal to its
original number.  The First Appellate Court shall now
proceed to hear the First Appeal by issuing notice to
the defendant(s) and shall hear the parties only on
the issue relating to the mesne profits.
8. With  these  observations,  the  appeal  stands
allowed.
9. Pending  interlocutory  application(s),  if  any,
is/are disposed of.

IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA 
CIVIL APPELLATE JURISDICTION 
CIVIL APPEAL No. 1105 OF 2019
MAGASVARGIYA SHIKSHAN SANSTHA 
THROUGH ITS PRESIDENT KAILAS 
S/O MANIKRAO GAVHAD & ANR. APPELLANTS
                                VERSUS
BHAUSAHEB SONAJI KAKADE & ORS.                     RESPONDENTS
   
O R D E R
1. This appeal, by special leave granted on 21 st January, 2019, is directed
against the judgment and order dated 6 th May, 2016 passed by a learned Judge
of the High Court of Judicature at Bombay, Bench at Aurangabad, allowing the
writ petition of the first respondent.
2. The operative part of the impugned order reads as follows:
“91. Therefore,  Appeal  No.5/2013  stands  partly  allowed  only  to  the
extent of directing the petitioners to reinstate the appellant / employee
as an Assistant Teacher on probation, so as to discharge his duties as a
Probationer for the remainder period of 2 months from the date he is
reinstated.  After  the  completion  of  the  2  months  of  probation,  the
petitioner / management shall take a decision considering the overall
performance of the appellant / employee of 2 years as a probationer in
accordance with the requirements of the 1977 Act and 1981 Rules and
pass, necessarily, a reasoned order with regard to whether the appellant
employee deserves to be confirmed in service. Needless to state that
the  petitioners  shall  consider  the  total  performance  of  the
appellant/employee as a probationer from 2.8.2008 till 19.4.2010 and
the further two months of probation as directed hereinabove.
92. Considering the peculiar facts of this case, the appellant/employee,
if is aggrieved by the decision of the petitioners, which shall be forthwith
communicated to him in writing, immediately after the conclusion of his
remainder period of probation, he shall be at liberty to take recourse to
the available legal remedy for questioning the legality of the decision of
the management.
93. Rule is made partly absolute in the above terms.  No order as to
costs.”
3. Although the appellants had laid challenge to the said order and even
special leave to appeal therefrom was granted, the directions contained therein

--- Page 444 ---
2
were implemented. The first respondent was reinstated in service, allowed to
serve the remainder period of probationary service and at the end thereof,
discharged from service.
4. Mr.  Sandeep  Sudhakar  Deshmukh,  learned  counsel  appearing  for  the
appellants,  submits  that  neither  the  order  dated  6 th May,  2016  nor  the
subsequent order of discharge was challenged by the first respondent in any
proceeding. 
5. Mr. Adgaonkar, learned counsel for the first respondent, does not dispute
that he did not challenge the order dated 6 th May, 2016. However, for want of
instructions, he is not in a position to apprise this Court as to whether the
subsequent order of discharge has been laid to challenge or not. 
6. The position that undisputedly emerges is that the order dated 6 th May,
2016 directing reinstatement of the first respondent in service and thereafter to
consider whether he should be confirmed in service or not, has attained finality.
In such view of the matter, nothing further survives for decision in this appeal;
the same stands disposed of keeping the question of law, if any, open.
7. Pending interlocutory application(s), if any, shall stand disposed of.

   UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. These Special Leave Petitions are filed against the Judgment
and Order passed by the High Court on 07.04.2022, by which the High
Court did not permit the petitioners to participate in the contempt
proceedings.
2. Mr. Shekhar Naphade, learned senior counsel appearing for
Respondents Nos. 2 to 4, has fairly submitted that the petitioners
could be permitted to participate in the contempt proceedings, on
which he will have no objection.
3. Having considered the matter in detail, we are of the opinion
that interests of justice will be subserved if the petitioners are
permitted to participate in the contempt proceedings.  At the same
time, we would allow the respondents to raise objections, as may be
permissible in law.
4. A bench of this Court while entertaining the Special Leave
Petition had granted an interim order on 14.07.2022 directing
maintenance of  status  quo . The said order is operative.  We,
therefore, direct that the said order shall continue till the High

--- Page 451 ---
3
Court disposes of the contempt proceedings.
5. The High Court may take up and dispose of the contempt
proceedings on its own merits as expeditiously as possible.  
5. We make it clear that we have not expressed any opinion on the
merits of the matter.  
6. In view of above, the Special Leave Petitions are disposed of.
Pending interlocutory application(s), if any, is/are disposed of.

JAMUNA BEHERA                                      Petitioner(s)

CORAM :  HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE UJJAL BHUYAN

                   Ms. Amruta Padhi, Adv.                   
                   
          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. Leave granted.
1

--- Page 471 ---
2. We have heard learned counsel for the parties.
3. Appellant was convicted by the Court of Ad-hoc
Additional  Sessions  Judge,  FTC,  Nayagarh  under
Section 302 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (for
short, ‘IPC’) and sentenced to undergo imprisonment
for life with fine.
4. Appeal filed by the appellant before the High
Court of Orissa at Cuttack (briefly ‘the High Court’
hereinafter) came to be rejected.
5. On 20.07.2026, this Court, while condoning the
delay, had issued notice, both on the Special Leave
Petition as well as on the prayer for bail.
6. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that in
the appeal before the High Court, appellant was
granted  bail.  As  per  the  custody  certificate,
appellant  has  undergone  more  than  10  years  of
incarceration.
7. Learned counsel representing the respondent-State
of Odisha submits that the incident is gruesome.
Appellant has been convicted for the murder of a
child. Practice of witchcraft or witch-hunting as a
motive has been attributed for commission of the
offence.
8. While we appreciate the view expressed by learned
counsel for the respondent-State of Odisha, we are,
however, of the view that, howsoever gruesome a
crime may be, the conviction must be based on sound
2

--- Page 472 ---
and credible evidence.
9. In the present case, the conviction is based
entirely on circumstantial evidence.
10. Without expressing any opinion on merit at this
stage, but considering the fact that appellant has
undergone more than 10 years of incarceration, we
feel that appellant may be enlarged on bail during
pendency of the Criminal Appeal before this Court.
11. Consequently, we direct that appellant shall be
released  from  jail  custody  on  usual  terms  and
conditions.
12. Registry to call for the records of the Trial
Court as well as of the High Court.
13. List the appeal for hearing in due course.
(ABHINAV KUMAR)                                (CHETNA BALOONI)
COURT MASTER (SH)                             COURT MASTER (NSH)
3

          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. The petitioner has been denied anticipatory bail by the
High Court in connection with FIR No 202/2025 registered
at PS Model Town, District Hoshiarpur for the offence
punishable  under  Section  108  of  the  Bharatiya  Nyaya
Sanhita (for short “the BNS”). 
2. The allegation is that the petitioner along with her  co-
accused  son and  daughter harassed  and humiliated  her
daughter-in-law into committing suicide on 22.08.2026. 
3. It is seen from the record that death did not occur in the
matrimonial house and there is also a statement that the
deceased had informed her mother and brother that she had
consumed poison. The fact that it was a suicide is beyond
dispute.  On a prima facie  consideration of the material
on record, we are of the opinion that the petitioner can
be released on anticipatory bail. We order that in the
event of arrest of the petitioner in connection with the
offence enumerated above, she shall be released on bail,
SLP (Crl.)  No.17686/2026                             2

--- Page 502 ---
subject  to  such  terms  and  conditions  that  the
Investigating Officer (for short “I.O.”) may deem fit to
impose, on condition also of continued cooperation in the
investigation. 
4. Once the petitioner is released on bail by the I.O., on
directions issued by the I.O. or summons issued by the
jurisdictional court, the petitioner shall appear before
the jurisdictional court and furnish bail bonds and ensure
due appearance in the trial. 
5. With the aforesaid, the petition stands disposed of. 
6. Pending application(s), if any, also stand disposed of.

[Arising out of impugned final judgment and order dated  17-08-2026
in CRLMC No. 5942/2026 passed by the High Court of Delhi at New

BHARAT CHUGH                                       Petitioner(s)

IA No. 270783/2026 - EXEMPTION FROM FILING C/C OF THE IMPUGNED
JUDGMENT
 
Date : 23-09-2026 This matter was called on for hearing today.
CORAM : 
         HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE MANOJ MISRA
         HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE VIJAY BISHNOI
For Petitioner(s) : 
                   Mr. Pritish Sabharwal, Adv.
                   Mr. Sandeep Mishra, Adv.

                   Mr. Surbhit Nandan, Adv.

                   Ms. Chitra Chanda, Adv.
                   
                   
For Respondent(s) : 
1

--- Page 513 ---
       UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. The submission on behalf of the petitioner is that
while considering the application of the petitioner to
lead  defence  evidence,  the  High  Court  mistook  the
application as one under Section 311 of the Code of
Criminal Procedure, 1973 when it would be one under
Section 254(1) read with Section 262 of Cr.P.C.  It is
submitted that summary trials are to be tried as a
summons case.  Under Section 254(1) of Cr.P.C., the
Magistrate  is  required  to  proceed  to  hear  the
prosecution and  take all such evidence as may be
produced in support of the prosecution, and also to
hear the accused and take all such evidence as he
produces in his defence.  At such a stage, the
Court has no discretion to refuse/deny examination
of  defence  witnesses  on  the  ground  of  their
relevance.  Though question of relevance would come
when a witness is being recalled in exercise of
power under Section 311 Cr.P.C.  Besides, the
judgments which have been relied by the High Court
are all in the context of exercise of power under
Section 311 Cr.P.C. whereas the judgment which
specifically covers the issue, namely, T. Nagappa
vs.  Y.R.  Muralidhar ,  (2008)  5  SCC  633  though
2

--- Page 514 ---
noticed has not been applied.
2. Issue notice, returnable in four weeks.
3. In the meantime, further proceedings of the
trial shall remain stayed.
   (KAVITA PAHUJA)                          (JAYANT RAJ KATYAL)
ASTT. REGISTRAR-cum-PS                        BRANCH OFFICER
3

--- Page 515 ---

O R D E R
1. This transfer petition has been filed by the petitioner
husband seeking transfer of Criminal Complaint bearing COMA No.
8082 of 2024 titled as Geetanjali Chadha vs. Amit Chadha & Ors.
from the Court of the Judicial Magistrate First Class (JMFC),
Ludhiana Courts, Punjab to the court of the Juidicial Magistrate
First Class (JMFC), Gurugram, Haryana and HMA/1137/2024 titled as
Geetanjali Chadha vs. Amit Chadha  from the court of the Principal
Judge, Family Courts, Ludhiana, Punjab to the court of the
Principal Judge, Family Courts, Gurugram, Haryana.
2. Since Ludhiana (Punjab) and Gurugram (Haryana) both the
places fall within the territorial jurisdiction of the High Court
of Punjab & Haryana at Chandigarh, therefore, in our view, this
transfer petition is not entertainable.  However, the petitioner
is at liberty to take recourse before the High Court.

--- Page 522 ---
2
3. In view of the above, we are not inclined to entertain
the present transfer petitions.  Accordingly, the transfer
petitions are dismissed.  Pending applications, if any,
shall stand disposed of.
